title: Verdier-duality exchange
statement:
Fix the global finite-field and coefficient datum of [sk-def-sf-setting], with $k=\overline{\mathbf F}_q$, $\ell\ne\operatorname{char}k$ and $\Lambda\in\{A_{E,n},\mathcal O_E,E,\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell\}$. Let $X,Y$ be separated finite-type $k$-schemes, let $f:X\to Y$ be a separated finite-type $k$-morphism, and put $s=\operatorname{Spec}k$, $a_X=a_Y\circ f$. Use the coefficient categories and operations of [sk-def-sf-operations], including its constructible exceptional adjoint $Rf^!$ in (vi), without an ambient exceptional-adjoint admissibility datum. Put
$$\omega_X=Ra_X^!\Lambda_s,\qquad\omega_Y=Ra_Y^!\Lambda_s,\qquad\mathbb D_T(K)=\RHom_T(K,\omega_T)\quad(T=X,Y).$$
Then $Rf^!\omega_Y\cong\omega_X$, and for every $M\in\Dctf(X,\Lambda)$ there is a canonical isomorphism
$$\varepsilon_{f,M}:\mathbb D_Y(Rf_!M)\xrightarrow{\sim}Rf_*\mathbb D_X(M)$$
in $D^+(Y,\Lambda)$, natural in $M$ and compatible with finite reduction, scalar extension and shifts. At the integral stage the coefficients are derived complete, and at the field stages the operations and comparisons are their rationalized and common-finite-stage forms. Coefficient compatibility means commutativity with the specified operation comparison maps on their stated domains; it asserts no extra coefficient-change isomorphism on arbitrary ambient inputs.

proof.text: The unit $\Lambda_s$ is constructible with Tor interval $[0,0]$: tensoring with the rank-one constant complex is the identity; integral reductions and scalar images give the higher-stage unit [sk-def-sf-setting]. The constructible functor types in [sk-def-sf-operations](vi) therefore put $\omega_X,\omega_Y$ in $\Dctf$. Apply [lem-sf-constructible-exceptional-compositor] to $g=a_Y$, $x=a_X$ and evaluate its conjugate at $\Lambda_s$. This gives the specified isomorphism $c_\Lambda:Rf^!\omega_Y\xrightarrow{\sim}\omega_X$.

Apply [sk-thm-sf-tensor-hom] to $M$ and $N=\omega_Y$, with the membership checked in step 1. Invert that exchange and postcompose by $c_\Lambda$ through the internal-Hom bifunctor [sk-def-sf-operations](i):
$$\mathbb D_Y(Rf_!M)\xrightarrow{\sim}Rf_*\RHom_X(M,Rf^!\omega_Y)\xrightarrow{Rf_*\RHom_X(M,c_\Lambda)}Rf_*\mathbb D_XM.$$
Define $\varepsilon_{f,M}$ by this composite. Both arrows are isomorphisms in the stated $D^+(Y,\Lambda)$; the second is a functor applied to an isomorphism.

For $u:M\to M'$, naturality of [sk-thm-sf-tensor-hom] gives the first arrow's square. For the second, internal-Hom bifunctoriality [sk-def-sf-operations](i) makes precomposition by $u$ commute with postcomposition by $c_\Lambda$. Pasting gives
$$Rf_*\mathbb D_X(u)\circ\varepsilon_{f,M'}=\varepsilon_{f,M}\circ\mathbb D_Y(Rf_!u).$$
Under $\RHom(M[r],N)\cong\RHom(M,N)[-r]$, postcomposition by the fixed degree-zero $c_\Lambda$ is the shifted postcomposition. The first arrow respects shifts by the cited exchange theorem, so their composite has the required $[-r]$ shift law.

Use [lem-sf-finite-exceptional-compositor-coefficients] for finite quotients and ramified finite-free changes, and [lem-sf-adic-exceptional-compositor-coefficients] for integral reduction, scalar extension, rationalization and common stages. With $g=a_Y$, set $\kappa_T=b_{a_T,\Lambda_s}$ followed by $G_{a_T,\Lambda'}(C_s\Lambda_s\cong\Lambda'_s)$. Their equations and naturality in the coefficient unit give
$$\kappa_X C_X(c_\Lambda)=c_{\Lambda'}G_{f,\Lambda'}(\kappa_Y)b_{f,\omega_{Y,\Lambda}}.$$
Naturality of the internal-Hom/direct-image comparison maps makes this the coefficient square for the second arrow in step 2. Paste it with the coefficient square for the inverse tensor–Hom exchange [sk-thm-sf-tensor-hom]. This proves the claimed compatibility on precisely the comparison domains stated there; field reduction uses integral representatives as in the adic lemma.

split_report.statement_disputed: The original statement allows X=Y to be the affine line with doubled origin and f=id. Then f is separated finite type but a_Y is not separated, so Ra_Y^! is outside the domain of sk-def-sf-operations(vi). Corrected by stating X,Y separated, making explicit the structure-map domain intended by the dualizing-complex construction.
